summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for acute-on-chronic bilateral sacroiliac joint pain, worse on the left. He reported poor rehabilitation experience after a prior admission and worsening pain at home. Labs showed elevated inflammatory markers without signs of infection. Pain was managed with a return to Dilaudid, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and cyclobenzaprine. Prednisone 20 mg daily was started as a bridge to biologic therapy. Rheumatology recommended outpatient initiation of anti-TNF inhibitors pending infectious disease clearance and Quantiferon Gold testing. The patient improved clinically, was discharged home with home health services, and given a plan for follow-up and medication tapering.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis sacral and sacrococcygeal region
